## Summary

I implemented digits-only telephone storage with normalization applied before the uniqueness check.

**What was needed:** telephone input like `(613) 555-0100` had to be accepted, stored/returned as `6135550100`, and treated as a duplicate of an existing `6135550100`.

**Changes:**

1. **`src/main/resources/openapi.yml`** — relaxed the telephone validation pattern from `^[0-9]*$` to `^[0-9 ()-]*$` so a formatted number passes request-body validation instead of being rejected with a 400 before it can be normalized. (This regenerates the `OwnerFieldsDto` bean-validation constraint at build time.)

2. **`OwnerFieldNormalizer.java`** — added `normalizeTelephone(String)`, which strips spaces, dashes and parentheses to leave digits only (null-safe). This single method is the shared source of truth for both the stored value and the comparison key.

3. **`BuildOwner.java`** (POST) and **`ApplyOwner.java`** (PUT) — normalize the telephone to digits before the owner is persisted, so the stored value (and thus the `telephone` field returned by GET) is digits only.

4. **`RejectDuplicateOwner.java`** — switched the uniqueness comparison from the generic whitespace/case normalizer to `normalizeTelephone`, comparing digits-only on both sides, so `(613) 555-0100` and `6135550100` collide and produce a 409.

The two new `Cp11Tests` (`coreStoresDigitsOnly`, `functionalityNormalisedDuplicateRejected`) pass, along with the full suite (273 tests, 0 failures) — including the neighbouring telephone-uniqueness checkpoints (cp02, cp03, cp05) and the v1 controller tests.
